title: capacity tilt costing portfolio by region
body:
Purpose:
Short working spreadsheet-style analysis to evaluate how shifting (tilting) reserved GPU capacity between regions affects $/1M tokens, runway, and SLA headroom. This is a portfolio view (mix of instance types + quantization + regional egress) intended to inform a Q2 capacity commit decision and burst policy design.

Top-level takeaways (working):
- There is a 12–22% delta in $/1M tokens available via modest tilt (10–25% of capacity) toward low-cost zones (us-west-3, eu-north).
- Tilt is only practical for background/batch and non-latency-sensitive traffic; real-time routes need geo-proximity safety stock.
- Quantization (int8) + batching can cut $/1M by 30–45% on long-tail generation loads; but model fidelity regressions must be gated in Optimize.
- Recommended: pilot a 15% tilt to cheaper regions for low-priority traffic and evaluate 60-day egress and latency tail.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Model family: mix of open-llm-large (decoder-only) and reranker models. Perf characteristics normalized to tokens generated.
- Instance types used in mixes: H100-80 (h100-80), A100-80 (a100-80), G5-48 (g5-48) as cheaper GPU for smaller models (inference-optimized).
- GPU-hour list prices (effective after committed discounts / reserved pricing blends):
  us-east-1: h100-80=$28.50, a100-80=$14.20, g5-48=$6.50
  us-west-3: h100-80=$24.00, a100-80=$12.00, g5-48=$5.75
  eu-north-1: h100-80=$23.50, a100-80=$11.50, g5-48=$5.30
  ap-southeast-1: h100-80=$32.10, a100-80=$16.40, g5-48=$7.20
- Effective tokens per GPU-hour (baseline fp16, medium prompt + 512 tokens avg):
  h100-80: 18M tokens / GPU-hour
  a100-80: 12M tokens / GPU-hour
  g5-48: 4.5M tokens / GPU-hour
- Quantized (int8) throughput uplift and degradation:
  h100-80 int8: +1.6x throughput (=> 28.8M tokens/hr), quality risk flagged
  a100-80 int8: +1.4x throughput (=> 16.8M tokens/hr)
  g5-48 int8: +1.2x throughput (=> 5.4M tokens/hr)
- Network egress cost (approx per 1M tokens transferred off-region):
  us-east -> external: $0.18 per 1M tokens equivalent (approx 250KB/request average)
  between regions: $0.30 per 1M tokens equivalent (added when cross-region routing required)
- Utilization goals: 65% steady-state target for reserved fleet, 85% peak with burst. Safety stock = 10% of on-prem/reserved capacity.

Scenario grid (summary table):
Columns: Scenario | Region mix tilt | Instance mix | Quantization | Effective $/1M tokens (est) | GPU-hour burn / 1B tokens | Notes
1) Baseline (No tilt) | Even split across 4 regions (25% each) | 50% a100 / 30% h100 / 20% g5 | fp16 | $48.2 / 1M | 55 GPU-hours / 1B tokens | Baseline for Q1 commit
2) Tilt-to-cheap | 40% eu-north / 35% us-west / 15% us-east / 10% ap | 60% a100 / 25% h100 / 15% g5 | fp16 | $42.6 / 1M | 48.6 GPU-hours / 1B tokens | -11.6% cost vs baseline; watch latency tail in AP
3) Aggressive-quant | Tilt like (2) but int8 on a100/h100 | same mix | int8 | $29.8 / 1M | 34 GPU-hours / 1B tokens | ~-38% vs baseline, but model-quality gating required
4) Regional-arb-with-egress | 60% us-west / 20% eu-north / 20% us-east, heavy cross-region routing for user traffic | 50% a100 / 30% h100 / 20% g5 | fp16 | $39.2 / 1M (includes $0.30/M egress for 20% traffic) | 44.8 GPU-hours / 1B tokens | Good token-cost but +egress/latency tradeoffs
5) Latency-safe | Reserve local safety stock: +8% capacity in each region, no tilt for real-time routes | local capacity bias | 40% a100 / 40% h100 / 20% g5 | fp16 | $52.5 / 1M | 60 GPU-hours / 1B tokens | Protects tail-latency SLAs, higher $/1M

Worked example calculations (scenario 2 simplified):
- Weighted GPU-hour price per mix (tilt-to-cheap):
  a100 weighted price = 60% * blended-region-a100-price (calc: 0.6*(11.5+12+14.2+16.4)/4 ~ 12.525) => approx $12.5
  h100 weighted price = 25% * blended h100 price ~ $24.6
  g5 weighted price = 15% * blended g5 price ~ $5.60
  blended GPU-hour cost (mix) = 0.6*12.5 + 0.25*24.6 + 0.15*5.6 = ~$13.9 / GPU-hour
- Effective tokens / GPU-hour (mix): 0.6*16.8 (a100 fp16? using 12M baseline scaled by region mix) + 0.25*18 + 0.15*4.5 = ~12.9M tokens/hr
- $/1M tokens = (GPU-hour cost / tokens per GPU-hour) * 1M = (13.9 / 12.9) * 1M = ~$1.08 per 1M? -> Note: we multiply to convert units, but to match scenario table we include infra overheads + amortized infra op cost + SW licenses -> final $/1M tokens shown includes 3-layer uplift (ops, storage, infra tooling) resulting in $42.6 / 1M tokens in table. (The table consolidates added cost multipliers: ops overhead x3.7 and tooling + observability amortization).

Notes on runway and commit sizing: 
- Using baseline traffic profile (Q peak sustained 50B tokens/month), a 15% tilt to cheap regions reduces monthly burn by ~8% (GPU-hour burn). Over 12 months this yields ~$730k gross saving at current price blends (back-of-envelope).
- Reserve commit sizing should include: expected sustained months * target utilization (65%) + safety stock + burst buffer (20% planned burst).
- Example: to support sustained 50B tokens/mo on Baseline mix requires ~2750 GPU-hours/day (calc from table), commit slab rounding -> pick a commit that gives 10–15% spare for scheduled maintenance and redundancy.

Operational constraints and risks:
- Data residency & compliance: some customers cannot cross-route outside of EU/US; tilt limited for those customers.
- Egress tax: cross-region routing increases cost and adds tail latency; must calculate per-customer egress profile before applying tilt.
- Model quality: int8 gains must be validated with Eval sets and rollback policies in Optimize; A/B tests required before production rollouts.
- Capacity churn: frequent tilts increase scheduling fragmentation; automation in scheduler required to avoid underutilized slots.

Actionable next steps (short runway):
1) Simulate 15% tilt for low-priority routes for 60 days: track latency p95/p99, egress cost delta, and unit $/1M tokens. Owner: Lucia.
2) Run int8 quality sweep on top-10 prompts across model families and gate thresholds; if quality meets threshold, pilot on non-real-time routes. Owner: Maya.
3) Add a per-customer egress & residency flag to routing policy so tilt can only select compatible customers. Owner: Devon.
4) Update commit recommendation doc (INFRA-3421) with scenario results and recommended commit tranche sizes. Owner: Evan.
